key_insight: This review traces how materials information extraction has evolved from rule-based pipelines to multimodal LLMs and agentic systems that support materials discovery.
engineering_relevance: Automated literature extraction can populate materials databases and knowledge graphs, assist researchers, and support closed-loop discovery when integrated with autonomous laboratories.
method: Review rule-based, NLP, transformer-encoder, LLM, and agentic extraction approaches.
Examine extraction across text, tables, and figures.
Assess generated datasets, extraction accuracy, computational costs, and pipeline design.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a critical assessment of datasets, accuracy, and costs but reports no quantitative results and highlights scarce reliable benchmarks.
watch_item: Reliable sample-level linkage of structure, properties, processing, and performance remains an open challenge, compounded by inconsistent terminology across document modalities.
paper_title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
